text.tspan: Page 1, the title page
What the pen says, word for word, and what it means
SHOW THE BOOK, DO NOT LIST IT
“Graph representation of book”
Put a graph of the whole book on the title page, above the
title.
SHOW THE BOOK, DO NOT LIST IT
“can also go here”
Or at the bottom: the graph can sit at the top or at the
bottom of the page (Dinis confirmed the reading).
THE MAKING-OF OUT OF THE READER'S WAY
“[struck through] The first edition (2018)
is the only official version. This candidate
was written by the book's agents from the
ideas register and is for reading and
marking up. ... the title is Dinis's
decision of 19 October 2026 (decision 014).”
Take the process notes off the first page; keep only what
the reader needs (not signed off, the frozen file, the
licence).
THE FIRST PAGES SELL THE BOOK
“should be what is the Book all about”
The paragraph under the title says what the book is about.
THE FIRST PAGES SELL THE BOOK
“this paragraph buys more time from the
reader to continue reading”
That paragraph's job is to buy the next minute of
attention.
